disclaimer: Informational, not legal advice. Kavach does not file reports.

regimes.name: GDPR Art. 33 personal data breach
regimes.trigger: Personal data breach likely to result in a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms
regimes.applies_to: Controllers (processors must alert the controller without undue delay)

stages.name: Notify supervisory authority
stages.description: Without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware; reasons required if later

regimes.notes: Content read from gdpr-info.eu (unofficial reproduction of the Regulation); official EUR-Lex text not read. UNVERIFIED against the official source.

regimes.name: NIS2 Art. 23 significant incident
regimes.trigger: Significant incident affecting an essential or important entity
regimes.applies_to: Essential and important entities under NIS2 (as transposed nationally)

stages.name: Early warning
stages.description: Within 24 hours of becoming aware of a significant incident

stages.name: Incident notification
stages.description: Within 72 hours of becoming aware

stages.name: Final report
stages.description: No later than one month after the incident notification

regimes.notes: 24h/72h/one-month figures confirmed on the EUR-Lex page; the start trigger wording and national transposition differences were NOT confirmed. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.name: DORA major ICT-related incident
regimes.trigger: Incident classified as major under the DORA classification RTS
regimes.applies_to: Financial entities in scope of DORA

stages.name: Initial notification
stages.description: Within 4 hours of classifying as major and no later than 24 hours after awareness

stages.name: Intermediate report
stages.description: Within 72 hours of the initial notification

stages.name: Final report
stages.description: No later than one month after the latest intermediate report

regimes.notes: Taken from a secondary copy of RTS Art. 5 (OJ L 2025/301) surfaced by search; sources disagree on clock starts and weekend relief. Official EUR-Lex text not read. UNVERIFIED. Kavach computes only the 24-hour outer limit from first detection.

regimes.name: UK GDPR personal data breach
regimes.trigger: Breach likely to risk individuals' rights and freedoms
regimes.applies_to: UK controllers

stages.name: Report to ICO
stages.description: Within 72 hours of becoming aware; phased reporting allowed; explain any delay

regimes.regulator: Sectoral competent authorities (e.g. Ofcom, Ofgem, DWI, ICO for digital service providers)
regimes.name: NIS Regulations 2018 incident notification
regimes.trigger: Incident with significant impact on continuity of an essential service
regimes.applies_to: Operators of essential services and relevant digital service providers

stages.name: Notify competent authority
stages.description: Without undue delay and no later than 72 hours

regimes.notes: 72 hours recalled from general knowledge; page not read. UNVERIFIED. UK cyber resilience reforms may change this.

regimes.name: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident
regimes.trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
regimes.applies_to: SEC registrants (US-listed issuers)

stages.name: File Form 8-K Item 1.05
stages.description: Four business days after determining materiality; materiality must be determined without unreasonable delay; the US Attorney General may authorise delay for national security or public safety

regimes.notes: Kavach cannot know when materiality is determined, so no deadline is computed from findings (the clock starts at the determination, not detection).

regimes.name: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule
regimes.trigger: Discovery of a breach of unsecured protected health information
regimes.applies_to: HIPAA covered entities (business associates notify the covered entity)

stages.name: Notify individuals and HHS (500 or more)
stages.description: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery

stages.name: Annual HHS log (fewer than 500)
stages.description: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year in which the breach was discovered

regimes.notes: HHS page returned HTTP 403 to the research tool; values recalled from general knowledge. UNVERIFIED. Media notice also applies for breaches over 500 residents of a state.

regimes.name: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reporting
regimes.trigger: Covered entity reasonably believes a covered cyber incident occurred; or pays a ransom
regimes.applies_to: Critical infrastructure covered entities (proposed rule)

stages.name: Covered cyber incident report
stages.description: Proposed: within 72 hours of reasonable belief the incident occurred

stages.name: Ransom payment report
stages.description: Proposed: within 24 hours of making a ransom payment

regimes.notes: NOT YET IN EFFECT: the NPRM was published 2024-04-04 and the final rule has no stated effective date; reporting is not required until the final rule takes effect. Informational only until then.

regimes.name: Cybersecurity Act incident reporting
regimes.trigger: Prescribed cybersecurity incident affecting a CII or covered system
regimes.applies_to: CII owners (and entities covered by the 2025 amendments)

stages.name: Initial notification (verbal)
stages.description: Within 2 hours of becoming aware

stages.name: Supplementary details
stages.description: Written details within 72 hours per CSA form; secondary sources cite 14 days, conflicting

stages.name: Final report
stages.description: Within 30 days per CSA form

regimes.notes: Figures surfaced via search summary of the CSA form page; the Act page fetched did not state them and sources conflict. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.name: PDPA data breach notification
regimes.trigger: Breach assessed to be notifiable (significant harm or 500 or more individuals)
regimes.applies_to: Organisations under the PDPA

stages.name: Notify PDPC
stages.description: Within 3 calendar days of assessing the breach as notifiable (measured here from first detection as a conservative proxy)

regimes.notes: Secondary sources only; PDPC page not read. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.name: SOCI Act critical cyber security incident
regimes.trigger: Incident with significant impact on availability of a critical infrastructure asset
regimes.applies_to: Responsible entities of critical infrastructure assets

stages.name: Report to ASD
stages.description: Within 12 hours of becoming aware; written follow-up within 84 hours if reported verbally (sources differ)

regimes.notes: Law-firm summaries; ASD page not read. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.name: SOCI Act other cyber security incident
regimes.trigger: Incident with relevant impact on a critical infrastructure asset
regimes.applies_to: Responsible entities of critical infrastructure assets

stages.name: Report to ASD
stages.description: Within 72 hours of becoming aware

regimes.notes: Law-firm summaries. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.regulator: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)
regimes.name: Notifiable Data Breaches scheme
regimes.trigger: Eligible data breach likely to result in serious harm
regimes.applies_to: Organisations covered by the Privacy Act 1988

stages.name: Complete assessment
stages.description: Reasonable steps to assess within 30 days of suspicion; notify OAIC and individuals as soon as practicable once an eligible breach is confirmed

regimes.notes: Secondary summaries only; OAIC page not read. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.name: APPI leakage report
regimes.trigger: Leak, loss or damage of personal data likely to harm individuals' rights (e.g. sensitive data, unauthorised access, 1,000+ people)
regimes.applies_to: Business operators handling personal information

stages.name: Preliminary report
stages.description: Promptly, commonly described as about 3 to 5 days

stages.name: Final report (wrongful-purpose cases)
stages.description: Within 60 days where wrongful acts are involved; otherwise 30 days

regimes.notes: Law-firm summaries (Nishimura, Baker McKenzie); PPC guideline not read; a proposed exemption from the preliminary report was not confirmed. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.name: CERT-In Directions of 28 April 2022
regimes.trigger: Occurrence of a listed cyber security incident (Annexure I)
regimes.applies_to: Service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates, government organisations

stages.name: Report to CERT-In
stages.description: Within 6 hours of noticing or being notified of the incident

regimes.notes: Six hours corroborated by several law-firm summaries; the official Directions PDF was not read, and sources differ on the exact trigger. This is the clock Kavach already shows at /v1/compliance/cert-in-clock. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.name: DPDP Rules 2025 personal data breach (Rule 7)
regimes.trigger: Personal data breach
regimes.applies_to: Data fiduciaries

stages.name: Detailed report to the Board
stages.description: Intimate the Board and affected individuals without delay; detailed report within 72 hours (Board may extend)

regimes.notes: Secondary page reproducing Rule 7; breach obligations may only apply from a later compliance date (one source says 13 May 2027). UNVERIFIED.

regimes.regulator: Autoridade Nacional de Protecao de Dados (ANPD)
regimes.name: LGPD security incident (Resolution CD/ANPD 15/2024)
regimes.trigger: Incident that may cause relevant risk or damage to data subjects
regimes.applies_to: Controllers under LGPD

stages.name: Notify ANPD and data subjects
stages.description: Within 3 business days of knowing the incident affected personal data; supplementary information within 20 business days; small agents get double time

regimes.notes: Several Brazilian law-firm summaries agree on 3 business days; the Resolution text was not read. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.name: NCA Essential Cybersecurity Controls incident reporting
regimes.trigger: Cybersecurity incident at an entity subject to NCA controls
regimes.applies_to: Government and critical national infrastructure entities

stages.name: Notify NCA
stages.description: Timeline not found

regimes.notes: No reporting timeline found in research. UNVERIFIED (rule text unknown).

regimes.name: PDPL breach notification
regimes.trigger: Breach likely to harm data subjects or conflict with their rights (draft amendments would remove the harm test)
regimes.applies_to: Controllers under the PDPL

stages.name: Notify SDAIA
stages.description: Within 72 hours of awareness; written justification if later

regimes.notes: Law-firm summaries; draft amendments are proposals. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.name: Federal PDPL breach notification
regimes.trigger: Breach affecting data subjects' privacy, confidentiality or security
regimes.applies_to: Controllers under Federal Decree-Law 45 of 2021 (DIFC and ADGM have separate regimes)

stages.name: Notify Data Office
stages.description: Immediate notification expected; no fixed time limit published

regimes.notes: Secondary summaries say the Executive Regulations had not fixed a deadline. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.name: POPIA section 22 security compromise
regimes.trigger: Reasonable grounds to believe personal information was accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person
regimes.applies_to: Responsible parties under POPIA

stages.name: Notify Regulator and data subjects
stages.description: As soon as reasonably possible after discovery; no fixed hour limit

regimes.notes: Law-firm summaries; form SCN1. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.regulator: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (OPC)
regimes.name: PIPEDA breach of security safeguards
regimes.trigger: Breach creating a real risk of significant harm
regimes.applies_to: Private-sector organisations under PIPEDA

stages.name: Report to OPC and notify individuals
stages.description: As soon as feasible after determining the breach meets the threshold; keep records for 24 months

regimes.notes: The OPC page tried returned HTTP 404; wording from general knowledge. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.name: PIPA breach notification (Art. 34)
regimes.trigger: Leak of personal information (thresholds apply for regulator reporting, e.g. 1,000+ data subjects)
regimes.applies_to: Personal information controllers

stages.name: Notify data subjects and report to PIPC/KISA
stages.description: Within 72 hours of becoming aware

regimes.notes: Law-firm summaries; a 2026 amendment extending triggers could not be confirmed. UNVERIFIED.

regimes.regulator: Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD)
regimes.name: PDPO data breach notification
regimes.trigger: Data breach with real risk of harm (notification currently guidance, not mandatory; reform proposed)
regimes.applies_to: Data users under the PDPO

stages.name: Notify PCPD (guidance)
stages.description: As soon as practicable; no statutory hour limit

regimes.notes: PCPD page fetch returned no content; recalled from general knowledge. UNVERIFIED.
